chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibn Abi Bashir, from Mansur, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

A man entered upon him and asked, 'Have you come as a pilgrim?' He said, 'Yes.' He asked, 'Do you know what reward is for the pilgrim?' I said, 'I do not know, may I be your ransom.' He said, 'Whoever comes as a pilgrim, so when he enters Mecca, he enters in humility. And when he enters the Sacred Mosque, he shortens his steps out of fear of Allah, the Exalted. He circumambulates the House with a circumambulation and prays two rak'ahs. Allah writes for him seventy thousand good deeds, removes from him seventy thousand bad deeds, raises for him seventy thousand degrees, and intercedes for him in seventy thousand needs. And manumission of seventy thousand slaves is recorded for him, the value of each slave being ten thousand dirhams.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific spiritual rewards and blessings for a pilgrim who performs Hajj with humility according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), emphasizing that the spiritual magnitude of Hajj is intrinsically linked to the pilgrim's state of khushu' (humility) and mindful movement upon entering Mecca. The specific metric of 'seventy thousand' highlights the multiplicative nature of divine grace for those who combine ritual correctness with spiritual presence, a concept central to Shia hadith literature on the virtues of the Sacred House.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 12. And from the previous chain from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Ibn Abi Basheer from Mansur from Ishaq b. Ammar from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi al-Hassan (a.s.) who said: “

Every pilgrim should enter Mecca for Hajj with extreme humility. When he enters Masjidul Haraam, he should take small steps out of the fear of Allah. He should perform circumambulation of the Holy Kaaba and offer two rakat Salaat. Allah, the Mighty and Sublime would note seventy thousand rewards for him, wipe his seventy thousand sins, increase his position seventy thousand levels, fulfill his seventy thousand wishes and grant him the reward of freeing seventy thousand slaves each costing ten thousand dirhams.”
